title: CHAPTER 11: LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT LAWS RELEVANT TO BANKING

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Covers the regulatory framework under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 relevant to banking personnel.
Outlines the essential legal requirements surrounding the Payment of Wages.
Addresses statutory provisions and compliance regarding Gratuity for bank employees.

cells: Dispute between employers and employers, or employers and workmen, or workmen and workmen, connected with employment or terms of employment
Any person employed in industry for hire or reward for manual, skilled, unskilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work; excludes managerial/supervisory >Rs.10,000/month
Compensation = 15 days average pay for each completed year of service; 1 month notice or pay in lieu; no retrenchment unless laid-off compensation rules followed
50% of basic wages and dearness allowance for lay-off period
60 days notice to appropriate authority; 15 days compensation per year of service; compensation equivalent to retrenchment
Conciliation Officer; Board of Conciliation; mediates between parties to reach settlement
Adjudicate disputes; Labour Court for individual rights; Industrial Tribunal for industry-wide issues
Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946: rules of conduct for workers; must be certified by Certifying Officer

items: Questions often focus on the applicability of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 to the banking sector.
Key terms, definitions, and rules related to the Payment of Wages and Gratuity are critical for banking compliance exams.

cells: Wages must be paid on time; deductions only as permitted; wage period not to exceed 1 month
All employed persons; wages paid before 7th/10th of following month depending on number of employees
Government fixes minimum wages for scheduled employments; employer must pay at least minimum wages
State governments fix minimum wages; violation is criminal offence
Gratuity payable to employee on superannuation, retirement, death, or disability after 5 years of continuous service
15 days wages for each completed year; max Rs.20 lakh; formula: (Last drawn salary × 15 × years of service) / 26
Minimum bonus 8.33% of annual salary (or minimum wage); maximum 20%; calculated on earned wages
Establishments with 20+ employees; employees earning up to Rs.21,000/month eligible
PF contribution: 12% each by employee and employer; pension scheme (EPS-95); Employee Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI)
Establishments with 20+ employees; EPF Organisation manages; EPFO
Medical benefits, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants' benefits; employee 0.75%, employer 3.25%
Establishments with 10+ employees; wages up to Rs.21,000/month covered by ESIC
